safety_verdicts.content: Patient denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, palpitations, headaches, or visual symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated captures denial of SOB, palpitations, headaches and visual symptoms, but does not document denial of chest pain (gold fact includes chest pain explicitly).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the documented denial of chest pain slightly weakens assessment of cardiopulmonary “red flag” symptoms and may prompt unnecessary concern or incomplete risk stratification. In this abdominal-pain/urinary-symptom context, the likelihood of major harm from this single missing negative is low but can cause inefficiency or additional evaluation.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient to have a review in 24-48 hours if symptoms are not improving.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies review in 24–48 hours; generated only says 'follow up in a few days' without the 24–48 hour timeframe.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Replacing a specific 24–48 hour review window with “a few days” can delay reassessment of potentially evolving conditions (e.g., worsening UTI/pyelonephritis, appendicitis, or pregnancy-related causes) and thereby delay escalation of care. This could adversely affect outcomes if symptoms persist but the patient waits longer than intended to re-present.
